title: Review (Supported): on fresh seed 5 catalysis-induced condensates form from a uniform state (297 droplets at t=300), and stopping fuel regrowth at t=1500 dissolves all of them by t~1650 (224 -> 134 -> 1 -> 0) while the fed twin keeps 220 and the enzyme total stays exactly constant
summary: labkit runs of c23's world on seed 5 (256^2, t=3000), fed and with WORLD_P fork_t=1500 (kF=0 from t=1500), identical until the fork. Fed: uniform e plus noise at t=0, ~300 droplets by t=300 that coarsen by merges to 188 at t=3000 (210 persistent tracks, 0 splits, 104 merges). Fork: bodies 224 (t=1500) -> 134 (1550) -> 1 (1600) -> 0 (1650 on), fed twin 222 -> 220 over the same times; enzyme total drift 0.0 in both runs (counts.json; the fuel and product totals go to 0 in the fork). The droplets dissolve, their enzyme is not destroyed.

observations.E: counts.json: fork 224 -> 134 -> 1 -> 0 bodies at t=1500/1550/1600/1650 vs fed 224/222/222/220; enzyme total drift 0.0

controls_run.E: rerun/fork/seed5 (kF=0 from t=1500) vs rerun/fed/seed5, identical until the fork

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed; I did not rerun the local feed cuts (r=8.5/17/30) or the hold and chi=0 twins. Global regrowth stop is the weaker of the rubric's E routes; the claim's local cut covers the per-individual one.
